title: Interpretations, Models and Logical Entailment
quickIdea: An interpretation is one truth assignment; a model is an interpretation that makes the formula true. A set of premises entails a conclusion when every model of the premises is a model of the conclusion.
remember: Interpretation = assignment of true or false to every variable. Each row of the truth table is one interpretation.
A sentence with n variables has exactly 2^n interpretations.
A model of F is an interpretation under which F is true. F is satisfiable when it has at least one model.
Premises entail G (written premises |= G) when every model of all premises together is also a model of G.
Deduction theorem: premises |= G exactly when (premise1 and ... and premisen) -> G is valid.
Refutation form: premises |= G exactly when (premise1 and ... and premisen and not G) is unsatisfiable.
So an entailment question is a validity question in disguise - pick whichever form needs fewer rows.

example.prompt: P and (P -> Q) entails which of these: false, Q, true, P or Q, not Q or P?
example.work: P and (P -> Q) = P and (not P or Q) = P and Q, which is true only in the row P = true, Q = true. In that row Q, true, P or Q and not Q or P are all true, and false is not.
example.answer: Four of the five - everything except false.

gateAngle: GATE 2016 Set 2 Q.1 is this question with the answer 4. The efficient method is to simplify the premise set to its single model and then test each candidate in that one row.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: Does {p -> q, q -> r} entail p -> r, and how many models does the premise set have?
variations.why: The premises fail only at (p true, q false) and at (q true, r false), which leaves four of the eight rows. In every surviving row, if p is true then q is true and then r is true, so p -> r holds in all four models.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: A formula has 4 variables. How many interpretations exist, and how many are models of p or q or r or s?
variations.why: 2^4 = 16 rows, and the disjunction fails only in the single row where all four are false.

trap.what: Confusing entailment (a claim about models) with implication (a formula), and checking entailment in one convenient row.
trap.why: Premises |= G is false if even one model of the premises fails G. Testing a single row can only disprove entailment, never prove it.
trap.counterexample: {p or q} does not entail p: the row p = false, q = true is a model of the premise but not of p.

check.question: How many interpretations does a formula in p, q, r have, and how many of them are models of p and q?
check.explanation: 2^3 = 8 rows. p and q is true when both are true, and r is then free, so exactly 2 rows are models.
